name: Mission Basilica of San Juan Capistrano
history: Mission San Juan Capistrano's great stone church of 1806 was destroyed by an earthquake in 1812, and services moved to the small Serra Chapel. A new parish church, patterned on the 1806 stone church but not a replica, was built just northwest of the old mission. The first Mass in it was on 23 October 1986, and Cardinal Timothy Manning dedicated it in 1987. It became a basilica in 2000 and a national shrine in 2003.
arch: Designed by John Bartlett after the old stone church, with domes and a bell tower. Historian Norman Neuerberg designed the interior and painted much of its art.
features: The Grand Retablo behind the altar is 42 feet high, 30 feet wide and weighs 16 tons: carved cedar covered in gold leaf, made by 84 artisans in Madrid.
Next door, the Serra Chapel is the oldest standing church building in California.

look.d: The domes recall the vaulted stone church of 1806 that fell in 1812.
The tower stands over a parish that also runs a food pantry for hundreds of families.

fun: The Serra Chapel next door is the only surviving building where St. Junípero Serra is known to have said Mass.
journal: A new church shaped like the old one that fell. A golden retablo from Madrid inside.

quiz.q: What destroyed the mission's 1806 stone church?
